title: Nimzo-Indian Defense: the ideas
line: The bishop pins White's knight, so White's king's pawn cannot safely come to the center.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its queen two squares, into the center.
Bring the knight out. For now it stops White's other center pawn from coming to e4.

also.d7d5: That leads to the Queen's Gambit, also sound. This lesson goes on with the knight.

steps.text: Move the pawn in front of your king one square. It opens a path for your bishop.

also.g7g6: That leads to the King's Indian or the Grünfeld, also sound. This lesson goes on with the other pawn.
also.c7c5: That leads to the Benoni, also playable. This lesson goes on with the other pawn.

steps.after: White's knight comes out to guard e4, so that White's pawn can go there.

steps.text: Pin the knight. It cannot move without leaving White's king in check, so it cannot take on e4.

also.d7d5: That is the Queen's Gambit Declined, also sound. This lesson goes on with the bishop.

steps.text: The bishop can also take the knight at any moment. White's pawn takes back, and two White pawns stand on one file.
A mistake, not a usual move: White pushes the king's pawn to e4 anyway.
Take it with the knight. The pinned knight on c3 cannot take back.
steps.after: Black is a pawn up, and the knight sits in the center.

summary: The bishop pins the knight that guards the center. While the pin holds, White's king's pawn cannot safely come forward.
